assessment: Sauvola and colleagues define the function of Tomosyn in establishing release probability at NMJ synapses in Drosophila larval NMJs. They present compelling evidence that loss of Tomosyn results in increased evoked and spontaneous release. They further find that Tomosyn likely acts as a decoy SNARE protein independently of Syt 1 and Syt 7 to negatively regulate SV docking. The data are of no doubt interesting for researchers in the synaptic transmission field.
